In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the data obtained are in favor of a primary cosmic-ray flux that is dominated by light nuclei and is described by a power law in energy with a slope that is slightly softer than that of the spectrum of protons.
the experimental data on muons from extensive air showers can be explained by a flux of protons with a power-law energy spectrum and by the interaction model QGSJet.

the results obtained in this study indicate that the properties of the ultrahigh-energy flux are consistent with the assumption of the existence of anisotropy in the flux and the interaction of cosmic rays in the atmosphere.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the data obtained from the DECOR experiment are consistent with the standard model of hadron interactions, with a primary flux consisting of protons and helium nuclei, with a small admixture of heavier nuclei, and with the assumption that the primary flux is isotropic.
the experimental data are in good agreement with the predictions of the standard hadron-interaction model QGSJET 02.
the data obtained by the DECOR detector can be explained by a mixed composition of cosmic-ray particles with the fraction of heavy primaries decreasing with energy.

the results of the comparison are best explained by the assumption that the primary flux is composed mainly of heavy nuclei, and the interactions of cosmic rays with the atmosphere occur according to the model of inelastic interactions of protons.
